summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy, systolic heart failure (EF 35%), type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted for chest pain, shortness of breath, and leg swelling over two days. He reported a heavy central chest pressure worsened by breathing and coughing, along with a dry cough and orthopnea. Initial evaluation showed elevated BNP (3969), mild pulmonary congestion on chest X-ray, and stable renal function. He was treated with furosemide for volume overload, with improvement in symptoms and respiratory status. His ICD was checked and functioning properly, with no shocks but recorded NSVT. H. pylori testing was negative. He was discharged home with continued diuretic therapy, instructions to monitor weight, avoid salt, and follow up with his cardiologist and primary care provider.
